name: Indigenismo
summary: Indigenismo is a Latin American body of policy, writing and politics, mostly by non-Indigenous urban elites, that takes the place of Indigenous peoples in the nation as its central question. Its strands range from Mexican state indigenismo, which sought to integrate Indians into a mestizo nation through land reform, schooling and agencies like the INI, to Mariategui's Marxist view that the Indian problem is a land problem to be solved by ending gamonalismo. It rejects biological racism and colonial-style hierarchy while often being paternalistic and assimilationist in practice.
scope: Classic twentieth-century Latin American indigenismo, c. 1920-1970: Mexican post-revolutionary state indigenismo (Gamio, Vasconcelos, Saenz, Cardenas, the INI) and the Peruvian current (Gonzalez Prada, Mariategui, early APRA of Haya de la Torre). It excludes Indigenous-led movements after 1970 (such as CONAIE or Katarismo), Indianism, ethnocacerism and Chicano Aztlan uses. Because the strands differ, many economic and institutional answers are inferred and low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Manuel Gamio
keyFigures.role: Mexican anthropologist whose Forjando Patria shaped state indigenismo.

keyFigures.name: José Carlos Mariátegui
keyFigures.role: Peruvian Marxist who argued the Indian problem is rooted in land tenure.

keyFigures.name: Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre
keyFigures.role: Founder of APRA, the party Peruvian indigenismo was first tied to.

sources.title: Indigenismo
sources.author: Coronado, Becker and Pareja, in reference encyclopedias (Encyclopedia.com)
sources.usedFor: Thinkers, mestizaje, paternalism, integration, critiques and Indigenous self-representation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Indigenismo's state agencies delivered health and education to Indigenous communities, so extending public care to marginal rural people fits its welfare-minded reformism, though healthcare is not a stated theme.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Mariategui and APRA-style indigenismo attacked exploitative labour on estates and in mines, so higher wages for poor workers are an inferred sympathy rather than a documented demand.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mariategui blames liberal, individualist property law and foreign capitalism for dispossessing Indians, and Mexican indigenismo relied on state agencies rather than markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Early APRA indigenismo sought to nationalize foreign-owned enterprises, which suggests sympathy for public ownership of key industries, though this was not central to the cultural-policy core.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Anti-gamonal and land-reform agitation targets concentrated landed wealth; higher taxes on the rich are an inference from that stance, not a quoted programme.

unions-good.rationale: Mariategui expected Indian peasants and workers to organize in revolutionary class bodies; unions are inferred as welcome organs of that, but the essay centres on land.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mariategui argues liberal individual property law enabled absorption of Indian lands, and Mexican reform overrode large-estate property through Article 27 land redistribution.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mariategui criticizes foreign imperialist capitalism for colonizing Peru, and APRA indigenismo sought nationalization of foreign firms, implying tighter control of corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Indigenismo was about state provision of schools, land and services to the dispossessed, so cutting welfare cuts against it; welfare in the narrow sense is not discussed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mariategui values communal Inca-style ownership but the sources do not endorse worker-owned firms in industry; adherents range from socialists to reformers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Indigenismo never addressed counter-terrorism surveillance; as an anti-state-abuse and pro-marginalized movement it has no clear lean.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Indigenismo has no doctrine on recreational drugs, and some strands defend traditional coca use while mid-century reformers were often moralistic about it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not an indigenista theme; adherents oppose racism against Indians but a stance on speech law is not documented.

strong-leader.rationale: Mexican indigenismo grew under strong presidents like Cardenas, while Mariategui looked to mass organization; adherents are split and the sources set no rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Mexican indigenismo was carried out by state agencies (DAAI, INI) and aimed to bring Indigenous people into the national state, so it is firmly pro-state.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is not a topic in the sources; the position is neither stated nor clearly implied.

empower-police-military.rationale: Mariategui says police measures cannot solve the Indian question and that gamonal power corrupts local law enforcement; more security funding is therefore not a priority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No indigenista source addresses sex work; the position is unspecified and adherents are split between reformist and conservative moral views.

decide-locally.rationale: Indigenismo was centralizing in Mexico, yet later strands and critics like Bonfil Batalla demanded local control, so the movement is split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Gamio held that Indigenous 'inferiority' came from oppression and not nature, an environmentalist view of people that fits rehabilitation, but prisons are never discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; Indigenous family and community life is valued as culture but indigenismo made no claim about family as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Mid-century indigenismo did not address it and adherents range widely; no source supports a lean.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by indigenismo; the movement's adherents are split by religion and period.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mariategui calls a religious solution to the Indian problem outdated and anti-historic, and Mexican post-revolutionary indigenismo was secular, implying a small public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Indigenismo exists to remedy the subordination of Indigenous people; modern definitions stress inclusion and sometimes compensation for past wrongs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Indigenismo has no theory of gender and writers on it noted its own gender bias; no lean can be inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mexican indigenismo made Indigenous heritage part of Mexican national identity, valuing heritage though often as a relic of the past.

gradual-change.rationale: Mariategui says reformist half-measures such as schooling or roads are superficial and calls Indian hope revolutionary, while state indigenismo was gradualist; the strands split but the Marxist core leans against gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mariategui rejects the hope that Indians will be uplifted by white immigration and mixing, and sees no need for European blood, so immigration is no remedy; he does not demand cuts.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Indigenismo became international through the 1940 Patzcuaro Congress and later UN-linked indigenous rights work, but no source states a view on empowering the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Mariategui condemns foreign imperialist capitalism and APRA wanted nationalization of foreign firms, implying distrust of open trade; trade itself is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: Indigenismo was a strand of nationalism in Mexico and APRA's was anti-imperialist, yet it also had continental scope; global cooperation versus country first is not stated.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No source addresses military intervention abroad; indigenismo is domestic in focus.

open-borders.rationale: Indigenismo built national, mestizo identities around states and never advocated open borders, though it did not discuss the issue directly.

limit-growth.rationale: Indigenismo pursued modernization and development of Indigenous regions through economic and educational work, not growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: An anachronistic question for classic indigenismo; contemporary Indigenous movements are pro-climate action but the mid-century core is silent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; indigenismo wanted modernization for Indians but ties their problems to land and social structure, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; no inference is secure.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mariategui writes that the Indian's hope is revolutionary and that revolutionary thought must be socialist; Mexican indigenismo was itself a product of the Revolution, though state indigenismo was reformist.

experts-over-public.rationale: State indigenismo relied on anthropologists and officials, Gamio's study-then-decide method among them, which implies deference to experts; critics note its paternalism.

central-planning.rationale: Mariategui sought a socialist economy and Mexican state indigenismo was interventionist, but central planning is not discussed and strands differ.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mariategui's communal and socialist leanings fit it, but reformist indigenismo never took a position on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: The idea is not discussed; Indigenismo's land programme is redistribution and communal tenure, not taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: An inference from hostility to concentrated landed estates; no source discusses inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Not a topic; indigenismo favoured land and schooling, not cash transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Anti-imperialist APRA and Mexican nationalist economics favoured shielding national industry, so tariffs are inferred as acceptable; not explicitly discussed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mexican state indigenismo directed economic and educational development in Indigenous regions through the INI, and APRA sought national control of enterprises; strategic industry is inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cuzco indigenistas favoured small holdings over big estates and Pimentel favoured private ownership, yet Mariategui championed communal land; strands are split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mariategui is socialist but the essay seeks land reform, not abolition of wages; a literal abolition is beyond the stated programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not discussed; a state-minded movement has no reason to want money left to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Post-revolutionary Mexican state structures organized peasants and workers corporately, but indigenismo documents say nothing explicit on wage bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: APRA was a dominant party and Mexico became one-party dominated, but indigenismo as a doctrine never asked for single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Indigenismo critiques colonial hierarchy and is republican in all its strands; hereditary monarchy is alien to it.

democracy-best.rationale: Indigenismo was integral to republican nation-building and APRA became a major party, but sources record state paternalism, not a democracy doctrine.

direct-votes.rationale: Not discussed in classical indigenismo; later participatory indigenismo concerned Indigenous congresses rather than referenda.

workers-councils.rationale: Mariategui expected an Indian proletariat to rally under socialism but he does not specify councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Indigenismo aimed to integrate Indigenous peoples into the existing nation-state, not to break it up; later Bonfil Batalla wanted self-determination within the state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Gamio held Indians have equal intellectual capacity and that inferiority comes from oppression; Mariategui rejects racial explanations as imperialist.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mariategui accepts revolution as the Indian's hope, which implies political violence is not always wrong; state indigenismo was peaceable.

war-builds-character.rationale: No indigenista source praises war; Indigenismo concerns social reform and integration.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mariategui dismisses a religious solution to the Indian question as outdated and notes missionaries serve the gamonal, and Mexican post-revolutionary policy was secular.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mariategui says a religious solution is the most outdated and antihistoric of all; Indigenismo is a secular reformist politics.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Indigenismo looks to state law and agencies to protect Indians; Mariategui laments that local power makes laws ineffective, which means it wants state law enforced, not privatized.

military-superiority.rationale: Not discussed; there is no indigenista doctrine on military rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mexican indigenismo framed the nation as mixed Spanish and Amerindian, a mestizo nation rather than one ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mariategui's Marxist strand treats the Indian problem as economic, rooted in landholding conflict with the gamonal; state indigenismo did not hold this, so only a lean.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Land redistribution and social inclusion aim at material equality for Indigenous groups, but 'equality of outcomes' as a principle is not stated.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Mariategui wants lost communal land restored and Mexican ejido reform returned land to communities, but classical indigenismo seldom granted political authority over territory; Bonfil Batalla's later critique demanded more.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Modern definitions include recognition and sometimes compensation for past wrongs to Indigenous people; reparations between nations is a different question, so only a mild lean.

civilizational-union.rationale: Haya de la Torre's APRA envisioned a united Indo-America, but the idea is not about shared religion; the sources do not make this a doctrine.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mariategui's praise of Inca communism and rejection of individualist law imply communal values over self-interest as virtue.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not discussed; Indigenous communalism points one way and liberal rights-based reform the other.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Indigenous cosmovision is often cited for valuing nature, but classic indigenismo by non-Indigenous elites rarely stated it.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; Mexican nation-building celebrated population growth through mixing and Indian advancement, and population control was not an indigenista goal.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Indigenismo sought modernization for the Indian; it was not anti-industrial, though it recognized costs from modernization that destroyed livelihoods.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not stated; indigenismo favoured modernization but cared more about equity than technological speed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Mid-century indigenismo predates this debate and its sources say nothing on bodily enhancement, so neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic for a movement of the 1920s to 1970s; no stance on algorithmic decision-making is documented.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; no inference is secure.

restore-past-order.rationale: Indigenismo sought change, not restoration, and condemned the colonial and gamonal order; some romanticized the Inca past though, so only a lean.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Gamio's empirical approach of study first fits pragmatism, but Mariategui was explicitly ideological; strands are split.

direct-action.rationale: Mariategui expected Indian organization and revolution, while state indigenismo worked through institutions; the movement is split on method.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources on indigenismo give no view on whether methods must mirror aims; state agencies and revolutionaries alike used it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Indigenismo sought land reform and schooling for farming peasants, and Mariategui praised the Inca agrarian system; a hunter-gatherer return is unthinkable.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of any indigenista programme, even Mariategui's, which stops at land and socialism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mariategui's communism leans that way, but his essay does not state distribution by need and reformists did not hold it.

production-for-use.rationale: Mariategui's socialist strand and praise of Inca communism lean toward production for needs, while reformist indigenismo does not state it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mariategui analyses exploitation by gamonales and foreign capital, but the general Marxist claim about profit is not made in the essay and state indigenists did not hold it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Mariategui expects an Indian proletariat to await its Lenin but does not set out a proletarian dictatorship; mainstream indigenismo rejects it.

collective-farming.rationale: Mariategui praises communal Inca agriculture and communal landholding, while Cuzco indigenistas and others prefer small private holdings, so the movement is genuinely split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not discussed; Mariategui critiques imperialist capitalism but the essay makes no claim about great-power war.

taxation-theft.rationale: A movement that relies on state programmes and land redistribution rejects the idea that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Indigenismo is about land, culture and inclusion, and no source ties it to a liberal harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Mariategui blames individualist legislation for absorbing communal Indian lands, and later Indigenous rights are claimed collectively as peoples.

conscription.rationale: Neither Mariategui nor the Mexican state agencies discuss military service, so there is no documented lean.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Indigenismo seeks integration and voice for Indigenous people in the nation, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Indigenismo gave the state a social mission of educating and developing Indigenous groups, the opposite of a business model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mariategui argues schooling and legal rights are hollow without land and material means, a positive-freedom argument.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not discussed; critics note indigenismo was itself an intellectual elite project, but no claim about universities and media power is recorded.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mariategui calls the ethnic explanation of the Indian problem one of the most outmoded imperialist ideas, and Gamio held Indigenous inferiority came from oppression.

organic-representation.rationale: Not discussed; post-revolutionary Mexico used corporate structures, but indigenismo documents do not state this as doctrine.

total-state.rationale: State indigenism was heavily interventionist in education and economy but never claimed the state should direct every area of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Post-revolutionary Mexican indigenismo was part of a national regeneration project, 'forging a fatherland' in Gamio's phrase, but radical rebirth from decadence is not the framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not discussed; indigenismo is inward looking and anti-imperialist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Mariategui denounces gamonalismo, a feudal personal power, as the main obstacle; this is the system he wants to end.

bound-labor.rationale: Mariategui condemns the feudal gamonal system and its bound Indian labour and says it must be eliminated.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not stated; Mariategui treats the Indian question as economic, and some strands criticize elite knowledge, but there is no general claim.

universal-morality.rationale: Not discussed; Indigenismo defended Indian dignity on grounds of equal capacity, which suggests universalism, but it has no stated philosophy.

single-common-good.rationale: Indigenismo offers no theory of a rational common good; it combines nationalist, Marxist and reformist strands.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: This question lies outside Latin American indigenismo, and none of the sources touch it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are outside indigenismo's concerns, which are domestic Indigenous inclusion.

revive-national-language.rationale: Bilingual education began as a way to move Indigenous speakers to Spanish; later participatory indigenismo demanded Indigenous-language schooling, so there is partial support only.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Indigenismo's economic focus is land tenure and rural schooling; votes within large firms are not discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Indigenismo relied on state-run schooling (SEP, bilingual schools); vouchers are not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: A state-led development movement would not favour austerity; deficits are not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mariategui says reformist thought can no longer be liberal and must be socialist, rejecting economic liberalism as a base for freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Indigenismo sought legal and institutional reform; moral example of rulers is not part of it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-imperialist indigenismo supports national autonomy against foreign domination, but the sources do not frame it as a stated principle.

force-without-un.rationale: Not discussed; anti-imperialist leaning makes unilateral force unattractive.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mariategui dismisses religious solutions as antihistoric and Gamio-style scientific study of Indians shaped Mexican policy.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Indigenismo's beneficiaries were citizens of the same nation, so the immigrant question never arose in the sources.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Indigenismo wanted state help for the dispossessed without conditions; work requirements are not discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mariategui sees the gamonal-Indian relationship as one of exploitation with no remedy short of ending the feudal system; Mexican state indigenismo was more conciliatory.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Indigenismo celebrates heritage, especially pre-Columbian culture, so sacrificing it would be abhorrent.

dominated-front.rationale: Haya de la Torre's APRA proposed a united anti-imperialist Indo-American front against foreign domination.

workers-nation.rationale: Mariategui tied the Indian proletariat to socialist internationalism, not national lines; weakly sourced.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not discussed; indigenismo was itself called gender-biased but has no stated doctrine.

ban-interest.rationale: Mariategui's essay attacks land tenure and imperialist capital, not interest-taking, so no documented stance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Mexican indigenismo sought to bring Indigenous people into the national state, and Mariategui rejects racial explanations; the law-based separation of races is contrary to both.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Mariategui shows gamonal landholders controlling local law and state action, a class-instrumental picture, but he never states a general theory.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: An energy question absent from the indigenista sources; anti-imperialists might resist foreign extraction but this is not stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Indigenismo was about assimilating Indians, not immigrants; no source speaks to immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: The idea is a conspiracy theory absent from indigenismo and incompatible with Gamio's and Mariategui's rejection of racialism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the indigenista sources I read.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-imperialist indigenismo does not support spreading a form of government abroad; but Vasconcelos's cosmic race idea had a universal-mission air, so only mild.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Indigenismo has no gender theory; scholars say it was gender-biased.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mariategui shows gamonales and their local political bosses corrupting law, and Rama-type critics say indigenismo served mestizo elites; hostility to oligarchic elites is common.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Gamio and Mariategui both reject biological explanations of Indian inferiority, so eugenic ideas are rejected.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from concern for the oppressed and critique of police and gamonal abuse; accountability for past killings is not directly discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Mexican indigenismo was state-run through the INI and Mariategui demanded land reform, both far beyond a night-watchman role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mexican indigenismo made mestizaje the nation's founding idea and Vasconcelos's 'cosmic race' praised it, so discouraging mixing is the opposite.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Gamio asserted Indigenous people have equal intellectual capacity and Mariategui rejects racial inferiority claims; equal worth is the movement's baseline.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not discussed; a Marxist debate that indigenismo did not take up.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not stated; the term is from later decolonial discourse, though indigenismo did criticize colonial legacies.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Integrationist indigenismo wanted one nation under common law, but legal pluralism arose later; no direct source.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the secular Mexican strand opposed religious privilege, so restrictions are unlikely.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious-law issue with no counterpart in Latin American indigenismo.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Mexican post-revolutionary education under Vasconcelos and Cardenas was secular, and Mariategui calls religious solutions outdated.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet-era question of socialist state theory that the indigenista sources do not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Indigenismo seeks inclusion of Indigenous people in the nation, but state versions were paternalistic and rarely asked for consent as a doctrine.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balances are not a topic in Mariategui's essay or in the accounts of Mexican state indigenismo.

population-transfer.rationale: Indigenismo seeks to incorporate and raise up minority populations, not expel them.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Mariategui supports revolution and land seizures from gamonales, which conflicts with an absolute ban on initiating force over property.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Indigenismo emphasises solidarity and communal tradition over struggle between peoples; the Marxist strand stresses class struggle only.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No source discusses outlawing parties; APRA itself was repeatedly banned in Peru, which only hints at sympathy for toleration.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mariategui's analysis of gamonal power over Indians is an analysis of domination, though he does not use republican freedom theory.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not addressed in the sources, which concern land and the Indian's place in the nation.

vanguard-party.rationale: Mariategui's remark that the Indian proletariat awaits its Lenin points to leadership, while the reformist strand has nothing on vanguards.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Indigenismo centres Indigenous peasants, who were the poorest groups, and demands land and schooling for them first.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy with no bearing on Indigenous land and inclusion questions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Pro-labour sympathies suggest opposition, but strikes are not discussed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mariategui argues the Indian problem is rooted in land tenure, and Gamio traced inferiority to oppression, so institutions not numbers cause poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Indigenismo made Indigenous and European heritage together the basis of the nation, so diversity is treated as a source of the nation, not a threat, though assimilationists wanted homogeneity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in indigenista sources; the movement worked through parties and state agencies.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not discussed; protection of the vulnerable from arbitrary power is the movement's mood.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A state-interventionist, pro-poor movement would accept price controls; inferred only.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not discussed; mostly democratic strands do not call for party media control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not discussed; indigenismo works within republican states.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization is not an indigenista topic since its subjects were natives of the country.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not discussed in the sources on indigenismo.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Haya de la Torre's pan-Indo-American unity points that way, but sources do not state sovereignty pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Civil-military constitutional arrangements are not addressed in the indigenista sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not relevant; indigenismo does not take a stance on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Mariategui rejects religious solutions, and indigenismo is a secular politics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Marxist-Leninist debate; Mariategui's essay on the Indian does not take it up.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Indigenismo itself was a movement in art and literature, which argues against censoring it, though it is not discussed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mexican post-revolutionary politics embraced no-reelection, but indigenismo as such says nothing.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not addressed in the sources on indigenismo.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-imperialism points toward it, but alliances are not discussed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not an indigenista theme; would be inferred only from hostility to landlords.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not discussed; Mexican revolutionary peasants armed, but indigenismo takes no stance.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Indigenismo centres rural Indians and values their communities, but modernizing indigenistas wanted to bring development to the countryside, so no stated view.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No indigenista source treats border reunification, though Haya de la Torre's Indo-America idea is regional rather than national.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Critics said indigenismo was the work of educated mestizo elites, but adherents do not hold that view of themselves.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Gamio held that Indigenous traits should be studied to decide what to keep and what to improve, implying a hierarchy, while later indigenismo valued cultures equally; the movement is split.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources on indigenismo contain nothing about capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; indigenismo is about ethnicity, not sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular state schooling and scientific anthropology were hallmarks of Mexican indigenismo, which implies evolution not creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not an indigenista theme; the sources give no basis for a lean.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Indigenismo grounds national belonging in territory and mixing of peoples, not descent from citizens; no direct source.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Mexican state created bilingual education for Indigenous children in 1939 and later participatory indigenismo demanded schooling in Indigenous languages, though the early aim was shift to Spanish.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not discussed, and Indigenous religion was not the focus of the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian liberal theme that indigenismo does not address.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist indigenismo opposes foreign financial domination, but debt cancellation itself is not discussed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mariategui argues the republic's formal independence left feudal gamonalismo and foreign capital intact, so economic transformation is needed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; later Indigenous movements in Bolivia and Ecuador used assemblies, but classic indigenismo did not.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not discussed; adherents were reformers inside republics.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not discussed; anti-imperialist strands distrust aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic for the movement's period and outside Latin American indigenista concerns.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss how a head of state is chosen beyond republicanism in general.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Nationalist state-interventionism implies dislike for independent central banks; not discussed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: A Middle East negotiation question with no indigenista counterpart.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Mexican Article 27 land reform subordinated property to social need and Mariategui criticized individualist property law.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Mariategui's essay does not assess the Soviet Union's economic character.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic for classic indigenismo.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance mutual defense is not discussed; Haya de la Torre's anti-imperialist front is not a defense pact.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No indigenista source treats annexation or occupation law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Mexican post-revolutionary policy curbed the church and Mariategui sees missionaries as go-betweens for the gamonal; a general rule is not stated.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources are silent on whether the head of state should stand above parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not discussed; the integrationist aims imply a united state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Indigenismo is a republican, modernizing politics; Mariategui calls religious solutions outdated.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One-country-two-systems arrangements are not discussed in the indigenista sources.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A redistributive movement would favour progressive taxes; not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Gamio held Indigenous perceived inferiority came from oppression, and Mariategui rejects racial explanations in favour of land tenure.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mariategui laments that gamonal power makes law ineffective for Indians, an argument for rule of law, but he does not discuss rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: An anachronistic goal that mid-century indigenismo never considered.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-regime theory is not part of indigenismo as the sources describe it.

leader-cult.rationale: The sources do not discuss public honours for leaders; Cardenas and Haya de la Torre had followings but no doctrine of it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are outside the indigenista sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate about already-existing socialist states; the Indian-problem essay does not address it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mariategui puts land tenure at the root of the Indian problem and Mexico redistributed land through Article 27 and ejidos under Cardenas.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return after conflict is not an indigenista theme in the sources I opened.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not discussed; indigenismo has no irredentism, so a lean against.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Secular indigenismo has no place for punishing apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not an indigenista idea and contrary to its secular modernizing character.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed, though Haya de la Torre's continental unity hints at regional cooperation.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Haya de la Torre's APRA envisioned a united Indo-America, which overlaps with the idea, but the statement's kinship framing is not the same.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: State indigenismo integrated Indians; later participatory indigenismo demanded autonomy and Bonfil Batalla wanted a pluri-cultural state, so the movement is split by period.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Indigenismo seeks equal rights for Indigenous peoples in the countries they live in; this is the logic of integration, though the statement concerns diasporas.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mariategui's Marxist analysis roots the Indian question in economy and land tenure.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not discussed; the sources attack feudal landholding and foreign capital, not cartels as such.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank rescues are not a topic in the indigenista sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The movement protects minorities, so it would oppose unchecked majority will, though it does not discuss courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not covered, and scholars note indigenismo's gender bias.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Anti-imperialism points to autarky for some strands, but a colonial bloc is irrelevant.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic for mid-century indigenismo; trade agreements are not discussed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive systems under socialism are not discussed in Mariategui's essay.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not discussed; Mariategui saw revolution arising from the Indian masses and Marxist-Leninist organization, not foco.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mariategui seeks to end the feudal gamonal order and colonial legacies, which are hereditary privileges of landholding.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Indigenismo celebrated Indigenous heritage as part of national identity and taught pride in it, though a civilization-centred curriculum is inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mexican indigenismo was paternalistic, with the state acting as protector and modernizer of Indians, but it rejected ruling inferior races; adherents are split, so a mild lean against.

patriotic-education.rationale: Post-revolutionary Mexican schooling forged national identity among Indigenous children, though the stated aim was integration.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Indigenismo is a movement to correct Indigenous disadvantage, so ending preferences cuts against it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of the indigenista sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Mariategui says liberal capitalism failed to remove feudalism in Peru, so he is sceptical, but he does not discuss general crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: No indigenista source addresses a country's influence over former imperial territories; anti-colonial attitudes cut both ways.

delink-world-market.rationale: Anti-imperialist, but not explicitly delinking; no source.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Mariategui's essay on the Indian does not take up this Leninist thesis about workers in rich countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Indigenismo opposes racial discrimination, so freedom to discriminate is contrary to it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not discussed; protection of Indian rights suggests support, but state indigenismo rested on executive agencies.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaties dividing peoples are not discussed in the opened sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Indigenismo is a republican politics emerging from Latin American independence and the Mexican Revolution.

minority-veto.rationale: Indigenismo wants national-level reform that landholders would resist; a minority veto would block it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Mariategui sees revolt as legitimate against gamonal power; the right to resist unconstitutional rulers is implied but not framed so.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The sources do not discuss parliamentary versus other authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are not part of the indigenista sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the indigenista sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Much indigenismo, being an elite project of protection, acted on a duty of the privileged to the Indian, and critics call it paternalistic.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Indigenismo is a politically engaged movement of advocacy and policy.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school style critique is not part of indigenismo as sourced.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not discussed in Mariategui's essay, which stresses gamonal coercion and legal power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mariategui criticizes foreign imperialist capitalism colonizing Peru; a general world-systems claim is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources do not discuss reserving office for native-born citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: Mariategui and Haya de la Torre both sought a Peruvian road to change rooted in Indigenous reality rather than imported schemes.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not discussed; nationalist strands lean to self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are not discussed in the indigenista sources.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Mariategui called indigenista literature one made by mestizos and wanted Indigenous self-organization; classical indigenismo was run by non-Indigenous elites while later strands wanted Indigenous leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: European constitutional politics are outside the indigenista sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A Cold War comparison that the indigenista sources do not take up.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historical dispute outside the movement's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Indigenous heritage advocates question colonial symbols, but monuments are not discussed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-gap debates are not part of the indigenista sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence statistics are not addressed in the indigenista sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Indigenismo and Mariategui seek solutions fitted to Andean and Mexican realities, but they do not question Western institutions as such.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not discussed; civilian state agencies carried out the programme.

paid-care-work.rationale: Unpaid care work is not discussed in the sources on indigenismo.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duties are not treated in the sources, though Indigenous community life is valued.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service selection is not discussed in the indigenista sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not an indigenista theme.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are a council-communist idea; the indigenista sources do not discuss them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State-led social policy implies disfavour for privatized pensions; not discussed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Mariategui praises communal landholding and Mexico's ejido system tied land to communities, though not to all individuals.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budget powers are not discussed in the indigenista sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Early Mexican indigenismo moved Indigenous pupils into Spanish, while later participatory indigenismo demanded bilingual schooling; the movement is split by period.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Anti-imperialism and land reform imply limits on foreign land holdings; Mexican Article 27 restricts foreigners, but this is inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: This legal doctrine is not in the indigenista sources, though the movement addresses unequal outcomes for Indigenous people.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumption culture is not discussed in the sources on indigenismo.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-imperialist and anti-oligarchic stances suggest agreement; not discussed directly.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is outside the sources; anti-imperialism cuts against great-power meddling but not clearly here.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not discussed in the indigenista sources; anti-imperialist logic cuts one way, support for Indigenous NGOs the other.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth policy is not discussed in the sources, though Mexican nation-building celebrated mixed population growth.

residents-only-property.rationale: Residency limits on property are not discussed; Mexican law restricts foreign ownership but that is a different matter.

job-guarantee.rationale: A pro-poor, state-active movement leans yes, but no source states it.

democratic-peace.rationale: A theory of international relations absent from the indigenista sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Obligation to obey law is not a topic in the sources, which both defend law for Indians and endorse revolt.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism points to non-intervention, but the principle is not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the opened sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories are alien to a movement defending a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Legal marriage is not an indigenista theme, but the movement's reformism leans conservative on family law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not discussed in the indigenista sources.

local-production.rationale: Local food sovereignty is a later theme; classic indigenismo wanted development and market access for Indians.

informal-organisation.rationale: Indigenismo worked through institutions and parties like APRA.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; later Indigenous-rights movements invoke international law, which pulls the other way.

religious-nation.rationale: Indigenismo built a secular, mestizo national identity, not a religious one.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anti-imperialist indigenismo rejects submission to dominant foreign powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal distribution among regions is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mariategui does not distinguish personal from productive property in the Indian essay.

defeat-communism.rationale: Mariategui was Marxist and APRA leftist; but state indigenismo was not communist, so a mild lean.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not discussed in the sources; state agencies delivered Indigenous services in Mexico.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mariategui calls religious solutions outdated but does not make a claim about religion fading.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mariategui says liberal capitalism never overcame feudalism in Peru, though he sees it could have.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality is not discussed by Mariategui or the Mexican state indigenists in the sources opened.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare is not discussed in the indigenista sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not discussed; indigenismo concerned Indigenous languages, not loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty relations between states and Indigenous nations are not a feature of Latin American indigenismo as described in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mariategui praises communal systems; strands vary.

majority-settlement.rationale: Mexican policy aimed to integrate Indians in place, not to settle other groups among them.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: APRA presented a third way tied to Indian tradition while others saw it as combining modern economics with Indigenous traditions; Mariategui was himself a socialist.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Indigenismo grounds Indigenous claims in ancestral land, but does not state a general doctrine.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Irrelevant to the movement and opposed to its egalitarian norms.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not an indigenista theme, so no documented lean.

suppress-opposition.rationale: No indigenista source endorses suppression, and APRA itself was suppressed in Peru.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Indigenismo is secular; Mariategui calls religious solutions outdated.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic-law question outside Latin American indigenismo entirely.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An Islamist doctrine with no counterpart in indigenismo.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Later participatory indigenismo channelled Indigenous organizing through state congresses while classic indigenismo was elite-led; the movement is split by period.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not discussed; scholars note indigenismo's gender bias.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Mid-century indigenismo did not address gender identity, and contemporary adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life law is not part of the indigenista sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: APRA presented itself as beyond the usual divisions in some accounts, but the sources do not state it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Mariategui's Indian essay analyses feudal exploitation, not alienation as a concept.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Irrelevant to indigenismo and contrary to its inclusion ethic.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Indigenismo is a secular republican politics, and Mariategui calls religious solutions to the Indian question outdated.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; Mexican state policy was secular but dress rules are not discussed.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law issue outside the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: German-style ordoliberal compromise is not discussed in the indigenista sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: No indigenista source calls for ending armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Indigenismo demands redress of poverty, not trickle-down.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-imperialism suggests non-alignment, but no opened source states a position on military blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Republican and egalitarian; contrary to hereditary rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual banking is not part of the indigenista sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Foreign finance is inferred as suspect from Mariategui's critique of imperialist capital; the IMF era postdates his essay.

property-franchise.rationale: Mariategui's critique of the oligarchy and the inclusion of Indians in the nation rule out property-based franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is later than classic indigenismo and not in the sources.

reification.rationale: Lukacsian reification is not discussed in Mariategui's essay on the Indian.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mariategui's essay concerns land and gamonal power; ownership of presses is not addressed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law doctrine is not discussed, though Mariategui laments laws made ineffective for Indians by gamonal power.

racial-franchise.rationale: Indigenismo seeks inclusion of Indigenous people; Mariategui rejects racial explanations and Gamio asserts equal capacity.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for the period of classic indigenismo.

open-government-data.rationale: An anachronistic transparency idea absent from the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Indigenismo celebrated mixing of peoples and is secular, so a lean against restriction, though marriage law is not discussed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are a recent innovation, absent from indigenista sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not discussed in the sources, which treat religion as peripheral or outdated.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Mariategui argues concentrated landed power (gamonalismo) makes law ineffective for the poor.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not an indigenista theme in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mexican policy was secular but sources show no push to promote atheism, so a mild lean against.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: No source argues for abolition; Mariategui criticizes policing as a substitute for land reform, not policing itself.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociationalism is not discussed; indigenismo pursued integration within a unified nation.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mariategui rejects religious or missionary solutions and relies on structural reform; state indigenismo was state-led.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not addressed in the sources, though Mexican politics embraced no-reelection.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is anachronistic for the movement.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic and not part of indigenista concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Church offices are not discussed in the indigenista sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is not addressed in the sources, and scholars note indigenismo was gender-biased.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Immigrant voting rights are not discussed; indigenismo concerned native Indigenous citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Housing markets are outside the indigenista sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mariategui expected organized Marxist party leadership but the sources do not discuss binding party decisions, and reformist indigenismo ran through state agencies.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: APRA's early programme sought to nationalize foreign-owned enterprises and Mariategui condemns foreign capital, so blocking foreign purchase of strategic firms is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Indigenous peoples should be integrated into the national culture rather than kept apart from it.
missingStatements.rationale: Mexican state indigenismo aimed to bring Indigenous people into the national state and Cardenas spoke of Mexicanizing the Indian, though later strands and critics reject assimilation.
missingStatements.declined: Integration of Indigenous peoples is specific to this ideology and contested within it; assimilate-immigrants and national-cultural-autonomy bracket the question.

missingStatements.text: The nation is best understood as a blend of Indigenous and European peoples and cultures.
missingStatements.rationale: Mestizaje was central to Mexican indigenismo and Vasconcelos's cosmic race became state ideology, while Mariategui disputed that mixing was needed.
missingStatements.declined: Mestizaje as national identity is specific to Latin American nationalism; no other ideology would take a side on it as a general question.

notes: Strands differ sharply: state indigenismo was paternalistic, integrationist and pro-mestizaje, Mariategui's was Marxist and held land redistribution and Indian revolutionary agency central, and later participatory indigenismo and Bonfil Batalla's critique moved toward autonomy. Answers follow the shared core of land reform, anti-racism and state action.
